scope: VisaAtlas mock interview preparation for Nigerian F-1 student-athletes

official_context.abuja_note: Routine visa services in Abuja were realigned effective August 1, 2026.
official_context.important_rule: Treat official information as policy. Treat applicant interview experiences only as observed patterns, never as official embassy rules.

core_questions: Why are you going to the United States?
Why did you choose this university?
Why did you choose this major or program?
Who is paying for your education?
What are your plans after graduation?
undergraduate_questions: When did you finish high school?
What have you been doing since you finished high school?
What were your academic results in high school?
graduate_questions: What did you study for your bachelor's degree?
What have you been doing since graduation?
Why did you choose this graduate program?
How does this program relate to your bachelor's degree?
If this program is different from your bachelor's degree, why are you changing fields?
student_athlete_questions: When did you start your sport?
What sport do you compete in?
How many U.S. schools recruited you?
Why did you choose this university over the other schools?

full_scholarship: How did you get your scholarship?
What exactly does your scholarship cover?
Are there any expenses that are not covered?
partial_scholarship: How did you get your scholarship?
What exactly does your scholarship cover?
How much of your total cost is not covered?
Who will pay the remaining amount?
How will your living expenses be covered?
no_scholarship: Who is paying for your education?
Why is your sponsor paying for your education?
How will your tuition and living expenses be covered?
What is the source of the funds?

previous_refusal_logic: Have you applied for a U.S. visa before?
How many times have you been refused?
What has changed since your previous refusal?
Is your university the same as during your previous application?
Has your scholarship or funding changed since your previous application?
Has anything changed academically, athletically, financially, or in your study plan?
Do not invent improvements for the applicant. Probe only changes that are actually supported by the applicant's profile or answers.
school_change_logic: What happened with the university from your previous visa application?
Did your scholarship, admission, recruitment, program, or enrollment timing affect the school change?
Do you think changing universities changes the visa decision?
If the applicant says the school changed because of a previous refusal, ask what specifically happened after the refusal.
Do not assume changing schools was an attempt to obtain visa approval. Ask for the applicant's actual reason.
non_athlete_rule: Do not ask sports, event, personal best, or athletic recruitment questions to a non-athlete.
For non-athletes, focus on academics, university choice, major, funding, education history, and post-graduation plans.
consistency_followups: Revisit important topics later using different wording when appropriate.
For example, after asking what the applicant plans to do after graduation, later ask what they plan to do in the United States after school.
Compare later answers with earlier answers for consistency.
If answers appear inconsistent, ask a natural follow-up instead of assuming dishonesty.

routing_rules: Do not ask every question in this file and do not follow the questions in a fixed order.
Ask one question at a time and use the applicant's answer to decide the most relevant follow-up.
Use core_questions for all applicants when relevant.
Use undergraduate_questions only for undergraduate applicants.
Use graduate_questions only for graduate or master's applicants.
Use student_athlete_questions only when the applicant is a student-athlete.
For a full scholarship, use the full_scholarship funding branch.
For a partial scholarship, use the partial_scholarship funding branch and probe how the remaining cost will be paid.
For an applicant with no scholarship, use the no_scholarship funding branch.
If the applicant has previous visa refusals, use previous_refusal_logic and ask what has genuinely changed since the previous application.
If the applicant changed universities since a previous application, use school_change_logic.
The interviewer may generate natural follow-up questions that are not written verbatim in this file when they logically follow from the applicant's profile or answers.
Never invent applicant facts, scholarship amounts, athletic performances, sponsors, or changes since a previous refusal.
Do not coach the applicant during the mock interview. Probe vague or inconsistent answers naturally.
